title: Patty Melt
subtitle: Beef patty with caramelised onions and melted cheese on toasted rye
excerpt: A thin beef patty pressed flat and cooked hard, topped with sweet caramelised onions and melted cheese between two slices of toasted rye. Diner food at its best.
sourceNotes: American diner classic, popular since the mid-twentieth century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Caramelise the onions up to two days ahead and refrigerate. Reheat before assembling.

content.text: A patty melt is not a burger. The meat goes flat and gets a hard crust in a dry pan. The onions must be properly golden, which takes more time than most recipes admit. Do not rush either step.
Melt half the butter in the skillet over a low heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and very soft. Set aside.
Divide the mince into two portions. Shape each into a thin oval to match the bread slices. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Increase the heat to high. Add no fat. Press the patties flat in the dry pan and cook for 2 minutes without moving.
Flip and cook for 1 minute more. Place cheese on top of each patty and let it melt while the second side finishes. Remove from the pan.
Wipe the pan. Add the remaining butter over a medium heat. Butter one side of each bread slice.
Toast two slices butter-side down in the pan. Spread the untoasted side with mustard if using. Add a patty and half the onions. Top with the remaining slices, butter-side up.
Press down gently and cook for 2 minutes per side until both faces are golden and the cheese is fully melted. Slice and serve hot.

items.symptom: The patty shrinks and domes in the middle.
items.cause: The mince was not pressed flat enough.
items.fix: Press the patty as thin as possible before cooking and use the spatula to press it down in the first 30 seconds.

items.symptom: The onions are still pale after 20 minutes.
items.cause: The heat is too low or the pan is overcrowded.
items.fix: Raise to medium-low and stir less often so the onions make contact with the hot pan.

items.symptom: The bread burns before the cheese melts.
items.cause: The heat is too high for the final toasting.
items.fix: Lower to medium and cover loosely with foil for the last minute to help the heat reach the cheese.
